{"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T13:36:53.300Z", "parent_tool_use_id": "toolu_01LsCrL1DDkTZGc6kMPVwn5D", "uuid": "25290ec9-cb8a-4372-b9de-0d07e5f32e60", "session_id": "f6240345-706b-40cc-9f2f-79083812aa57", "agent_id": "a259b68ccd4223cbc", "message": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "id": "msg_011CgKFxkp5gihtuMhLfWFmX", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01AtPqkiXFSkQJdZrY3tBye2", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "cd /app; W=.spektacular/work/20260101000001-storage\ncat > $W/architecture.md <<'EOF'\nA single new module `todo/storage.py` in the todo-app repo exposes `load()` and `save(todos)`. The todo list is a `list[dict]` of `{\"id\": int, \"title\": str, \"done\": bool}`, serialised as a JSON array. The file path is resolved on every call (`TODO_FILE` env var if set, else `~/.todo.json` via `Path.home()`), so tests and callers can change the environment between calls and the real home file is never touched when `TODO_FILE` is set.\n\n`load()` returns `[]` when the file does not exist and otherwise parses the JSON; invalid JSON propagates the `json.JSONDecodeError` rather than returning `[]`, because silently treating corruption as empty would let the next `save` destroy the data. `save()` writes to a temporary file created in the same directory as the target (same filesystem), flushes and fsyncs it, then `os.replace`s it over the target, so the disk holds either the old file or the complete new one. On failure the temp file is removed.\n\nOptions weighed: (A) temp file + os.replace in the same directory (chosen, matches spec Technical Approach, Low effort); (B) direct overwrite, rejected as it can leave a partial file; (C) write backup then overwrite, rejected as still non-atomic. A todo dataclass was rejected as over-engineering: plain dicts keep the round trip trivially equal. See research.md#alternatives-considered-and-rejected.\nEOF\necho \"No project conventions apply to this feature; the knowledge base holds no conventions.\" > $W/conventions.md\ncat >> $W/assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n\n### Architecture direction (architecture)\n- **Decision**: temp file in same dir + fsync + os.replace; todos as plain dicts; path resolved per call\n- **Rationale**: matches spec Technical Approach; simplest equality round trip\n- **Rejected**: direct overwrite, backup-then-overwrite, dataclass model\n\n### Conventions (architecture)\n- **Decision**: none apply (knowledge base empty)\n- **Rationale**: always-applied returned no entries\n- **Rejected**: n/a\nEOF\necho \"Architecture chosen: os.replace temp file; no conventions.\" >> .spektacular/workflows/plan-20260101000001-storage.md\nspektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"components\",\"name\":\"20260101000001-storage\"}'"}}]}}

Handlers stay as small functions in todo/cli.py.\n- **Handlers print and call sys.exit directly** \u2014 rejected: handlers return an int exit status and main() returns it, matching main() -> int (todo/cli.py:16) and `raise SystemExit(main())` (todo/__main__.py:3). Testable without catching SystemExit.\n- **Using argparse type=int for id and letting argparse reject non-integers** \u2014 chosen actually (argparse exits 2 with its own message); an integer-but-unknown id is the exit-1 case in the spec.\n- **Allocating ids with len(todos)+1** \u2014 rejected: spec says highest id + 1 (reuse-safe if gaps exist).\n\n## Chosen approach - evidence\n\n- Spec Technical Approach: argparse subparsers in todo/cli.py; new id = max existing id + 1 (1 when empty).\n- Spec Constraint: only storage.load()/save(); storage plan (20260101000001-storage) defines todo as {\"id\":int,\"title\":str,\"done\":bool}, load() -> [] if absent, save(todos), path via TODO_FILE or ~/.todo.json.\n- Storage plan states invalid JSON propagates json.JSONDecodeError; corrupt-file recovery is left to this spec. Decision: not handled here (not in spec requirements); traceback propagates. Recorded as assumption.\n- todo/cli.py:12-18: main(argv) -> int with parse_args(argv); tests can call main([...]) directly with TODO_FILE set to a temp file.\n\n## Files examined\n\n- todo-app:todo/cli.py:1-18 \u2014 bare parser, main returns 0, docstring says no commands yet (to update).\n- todo-app:todo/__main__.py:1-3 \u2014 raise SystemExit(main()), so returned int is the exit status.\n- todo-app:todo/__init__.py \u2014 version only.\n- todo-app:README.md \u2014 says package is a skeleton; update to describe commands.\n- todo-app:todo/storage.py \u2014 does NOT exist yet; created by the storage plan, which must land first.\n- No tests directory exists yet; the storage plan introduces tests/ with unittest.\n\n## External references\n\n- Python argparse docs (subparsers, `required=True` on add_subparsers, type=int) \u2014 behaviour of exit code 2 for usage errors.\n\n## Prior plans / specs consulted\n\n- 20260101000001-storage plan: storage contract and unittest + TODO_FILE isolation convention reused here.\n- 20260101000003-help (sibling spec, in parallel planning): also edits todo/cli.py help text; keep subparser creation structured so help text can be added without restructuring. Spec says help text beyond argparse's generation is out of scope here.\n\n## Open assumptions\n\n- storage.py lands before implementation; if its load/save signature differs from the storage plan, implement must STOP and ask.\n- No-subcommand behaviour: the spec is silent. Assumed `required=True` so bare `todo` is a usage error (exit 2). If the help spec needs bare `todo` to print help, it owns that change.\n- Title with multiple words: `todo add buy milk` unquoted is rejected by argparse (extra argument); title is a single positional.\n- No knowledge entries, no design references exist.\n\n## Rehydration cues\n\n- `spektacular spec file read 20260101000002-commands`; `spektacular plan file read 20260101000001-storage plan`; read todo/cli.py and todo/__main__.py; `spektacular repo list` (root /app).\nEOF\ncat > .spektacular/work/20260101000002-commands/assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n### Bare `todo` with no subcommand (discovery)\n- **Decision**: subparsers are required; no subcommand is a usage error (exit 2).\n- **Rationale**: spec is silent; current bare behaviour (exit 0) has no meaning once commands exist; help spec owns any friendlier behaviour.\n- **Rejected**: printing help with exit 0 - overlaps the help spec.\n\n### Corrupt storage file not handled (discovery)\n- **Decision**: json.JSONDecodeError from load() propagates.\n- **Rationale**: not in this spec's requirements; the storage plan deferred it but silently overwriting is worse than a traceback.\n- **Rejected**: catching and exiting 1 with message - scope creep.\nEOF\ncat > .spektacular/workflows/plan-20260101000002-commands.md <<'EOF'\n- Storage module not yet on disk; plan builds on its plan. No knowledge/design refs. Decisions in work/assumptions.md.\nEOF\nspektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"architecture\",\"name\":\"20260101000002-commands\"}'"}}]}}

{"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T13:39:00.568Z", "parent_tool_use_id": "toolu_011gDQrdkhaFHQxGGBxQvxzo", "uuid": "e27f6c52-a1cd-47d8-b4e9-a14cd9322ace", "session_id": "f6240345-706b-40cc-9f2f-79083812aa57", "agent_id": "a2ea70506e1c21975", "message": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "id": "msg_011CgKG7tmZLHpLDDUZzpaNE", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_018iRwAcoc8PEPkcDjA21PPy", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "cd /app/.spektacular/work/20260101000002-commands; cat > architecture.md <<'EOF'\nThe three commands live in the existing `todo/cli.py` in the todo-app repo. `build_parser()` gains an `argparse` subparsers group (required) with `add <title>`, `list` and `done <id>` (id parsed with `type=int`). Each subparser binds a small handler function through `set_defaults(func=...)`; `main()` parses, calls `args.func(args)` and returns its integer exit status, which `__main__.py` already passes to `SystemExit`. Handlers read and write only through `storage.load()` and `storage.save()` from the storage plan, so persistence, the `TODO_FILE` override and atomic writes are not re-implemented here.\n\nBehaviour: `add` loads the list, assigns id `max(existing ids, default 0) + 1`, appends `{\"id\", \"title\", \"done\": false}`, saves and prints the id. `list` prints one line per todo, sorted by id, as `<id> [x| ] <title>` (a done marker `[x]` or `[ ]`); an empty list prints nothing. `done` loads, flips `done` to true on the matching id and saves; an unknown id prints `error: no todo with id N` to stderr, saves nothing and returns 1. Handlers return the status rather than calling `sys.exit`, so tests call `main([...])` directly.\n\nOptions weighed: (A) handlers as functions in `todo/cli.py` with `set_defaults(func=...)` (chosen, Low effort, matches the spec's Technical Approach and keeps the single-file skeleton); (B) a `todo/commands/` package with a module per command, rejected as over-engineering for three short handlers (Medium); (C) an if/elif dispatch on `args.command` in `main()`, rejected as it grows awkwardly when the help spec adds to the same parser (Low). Trade-offs: the exact line format and error wording are not fixed by the spec, so they are chosen here and tested; a bare `todo` becomes a usage error (exit 2), and a corrupt storage file surfaces as a traceback, both left to other specs. See research.md#alternatives-considered-and-rejected.\nEOF\necho 'No project conventions apply to this feature; the knowledge base holds no conventions.' > conventions.md\ncat >> assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n\n### Handlers as functions in cli.py, output format (architecture)\n- **Decision**: set_defaults(func=...) handlers in todo/cli.py; list line `<id> [x] <title>` / `[ ]`; error text `error: no todo with id N`; done on already-done todo succeeds idempotently.\n- **Rationale**: spec fixes only content, order and exit status; matches Technical Approach.\n- **Rejected**: commands package; if/elif dispatch; erroring on already-done.\n\n### No conventions apply (architecture)\n- **Decision**: none selected; knowledge base has no conventions.\n- **Rationale**: always-applied load returned empty.\n- **Rejected**: n/a\nEOF\ncd /app; echo '- Architecture: handlers in cli.py via set_defaults; see assumptions.md' >> .spektacular/workflows/plan-20260101000002-commands.md\nspektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"components\",\"name\":\"20260101000002-commands\"}' | python3 -c \"import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['instruction'][:3500])\""}}]}}
